FOUNDATION SWITCHBOARD

No fake absolute root.

The ambition to reveal every branch from its seeds is right. The phrase “absolute first principles” is the dangerous part: mathematics has several rigorous foundational presentations, and each still uses a surrounding metalanguage. QEVA makes the choice visible instead of hiding it.

CONSTRUCTIVE CORRECTIONThere may be no neutral point beneath every possible framework. QEVA therefore preserves a shared orientation floor, then branches into explicit systems. A translation between branches is stored as a mathematical result—not assumed because two diagrams look alike.

SHARED ORIENTATION FLOOR

The smallest useful corridor.

These are not declared metaphysical atoms. They are the recurring roles needed to state what a formal framework contains and how it operates.

01 · OBSERVEDistinctiontell one state from another 02 · REFERObjectadmit something as one thing 03 · WRITESymbolmake a distinguishable token 04 · FORMExpressionbuild legal arrangements 05 · ASSERTStatementform something evaluable 06 · GRANTAxiomdeclare a starting statement 07 · MOVEInference rulelicense a step 08 · CHECKProofreplay a finite derivation 09 · INTERPRETModelgive the language a world 10 · EVALUATESatisfactionask what holds in that world

FORMAL BRANCHES

Different foundations expose different machinery.

QEVA can host more than one without flattening them into vague equivalence.

CLASSICAL · SET-THEORETIC

ZFC branch

Objects are encoded as sets inside classical first-order logic. Membership is primitive; axiom families constrain which sets exist.

  1. language with equality and ∈
  2. classical first-order proof calculus
  3. extensionality and existence axioms
  4. separation and replacement schemes
  5. foundation and choice

Open ZFC node

Strength: a widely shared common foundation. Boundary: set encodings can hide the structures mathematicians actually reason with.

CONSTRUCTIVE · TYPE-THEORETIC

Dependent types

Terms carry types; propositions may be represented as types and proofs as terms. A specification can depend on a value.

  1. judgments and contexts
  2. type formation rules
  3. introduction and elimination rules
  4. computation and equality rules
  5. universe and extensionality choices

Open type-theory node

Strength: executable proof objects. Boundary: there are many dependent type theories; their equality and universe rules differ.

STRUCTURAL · CATEGORICAL

Objects and arrows

Structure is studied through maps, composition, universal properties, and invariance under appropriate equivalence.

  1. objects and morphisms
  2. identity arrows
  3. associative composition
  4. universal constructions
  5. size and logic supplied by a chosen foundation

Open categorical node

Strength: relations between whole mathematical worlds. Boundary: “arrows only” still needs syntax and a metatheory.

LOGICAL VARIATION

Classical and constructive

Even before sets or types, different logics permit different proof moves and give existence claims different computational force.

  1. excluded middle or its absence
  2. double-negation rules
  3. witness-bearing existence
  4. proof relevance or irrelevance
  5. semantic interpretation

Classical · Constructive

QEVA records the branch on every claim whose validity depends on it.

ONE BRANCH, OPENED UP

ZFC is not one magic word.

Its major axioms and schemas are separate, citable objects. The framework node depends on their exact revisions; alternative set theories can reuse some and reject or replace others.

IDENTITY

Extensionality

Same members force equal sets.

BASE

Empty set

A memberless set exists.

CONSTRUCTION

Pairing

Two sets can be collected.

CONSTRUCTION

Union

One membership layer can be flattened.

CONSTRUCTION

Power set

All subsets can be collected.

EXISTENCE

Infinity

An inductively closed set exists.

SCHEMA

Separation

Definable subsets can be selected.

SCHEMA

Replacement

Definable images remain sets.

WELL-FOUNDEDNESS

Foundation

Ordinary descending membership loops are blocked.

SELECTION

Choice

Arbitrary nonempty families admit simultaneous selection.

What an axiom table must show

LayerQuestionNever assume
SyntaxWhich expressions are well formed?That readable notation has a unique meaning.
RulesWhich derivation steps are licensed?That a rule is semantically sound.
AxiomsWhich statements are granted?That an axiom describes physical reality.
SemanticsWhich models interpret the language?That one intended model is forced.
TranslationHow does one framework interpret another?That analogy is equivalence.
MetatheoryWhere is consistency or completeness proved?That a system certifies itself without conditions.
QEVAA foundation is a declared branch, not hidden ground.
